## One-line answers

**Q1 — Does `Procedure Type Code` trickle down (constant within a notice)?**
**Yes.** It is constant within every notice: **0** of 3,123 `Contract ID`s contain more than one distinct non-null procedure code, and **0** of 4,668 `Award ID`s contain more than one across their contractor rows. A notice can never mix codes.

**Q2 — Can one notice mix competitive and non-competitive lots/awards under the same `Contract ID`?**
**No.** The co-mingling hunt returned an **empty list**: **0** `Contract ID`s contain both a competitive award (`open`/`restricted`/`neg-w-call`/`comp-dial`/`comp-tend`/`oth-mult`) and a non-competitive award (`neg-wo-call`/`oth-single`).

---

## Numbers from each check

**Check 1 — Procedure Type Code trickle-down**
- Per `Contract ID` (3,123 notices): notices with >1 distinct non-null code = **0**
  - Distribution of distinct-non-null-codes per notice: **0 → 194, 1 → 2,929** (max is 1)

- Per `Award ID`: awards with >1 distinct value = **0** (distribution: **1 → 4,668**)
- Overall NaNs: `Eu Funded` = **0**; `Procedure Type Code` = **324**

**Check 3 — Co-mingling hunt**

**Check 4 — Distinct procedure codes present (8 non-null values + NaN)**

| Code | Rows |

- "Distinct codes per notice" distribution: **0 → 194, 1 → 2,929** (no notice ever has 2+).
- `innovation` and `exp-int-rail` are **absent** from this dataset (consistent with solar awards; both are in the eForms codelist but don't occur here). Every non-null code maps cleanly into the competitive/non-competitive buckets — nothing falls outside.

**Check 5 — Partial NaN within an otherwise-populated notice**
- Notices (Contract ID) with BOTH some NaN and some non-null `Procedure Type Code` = **0**
- Notices **fully** NaN = **194**; notices fully populated = **2,929**

---

## Do the two flags behave identically?

**Empirically, yes — identically.** Both `Procedure Type Code` and `Eu Funded` are constant within every notice and every award in this flattened dataset: 0 mixed notices, 0 mixed awards, and 0 partial-NaN patterns for either field. Both are safe to de-duplicate at the notice (`Contract ID`) level.

**At the schema level, no — they are modelled differently.** This is the one nuance worth flagging:

- `Procedure Type Code` (**BT-105**) is genuinely a **procedure/notice-level** field in eForms (cardinality **1**, "marked for the whole Procedure").
- `Eu Funded` (**BT-60**) is technically a **lot-level** field in eForms ("used per Lot"), yet in this flattened export it is constant per notice (the official TED CSV subset collapses it to the notice-level `B_EU_FUNDS` column). So it *looks* notice-level in the data even though the underlying schema permits per-lot declaration.

So: **identical trickle-down behaviour in the data, but different levels in the source model.**

---

## Schema-level conclusion (with quotes)

**`Procedure Type Code` = BT-105 = a procedure/notice-level field, declared once per procedure — the schema does NOT allow per-lot variation.**

From the eForms SDK spec, "Procedure, Group of Lots, Lot & Part related information" (the exact page cited as source #11 in `ted-fields-reference.md`):

> "**Procedure Type (BT-105)** | [Procedure Type (BT-105)] | **1** | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | `cbc:ProcedureCode`" *(Table 7 — Tendering Process)*

The cardinality **"1"** sits in the **Procedure** column (mandatory & unique — exactly one per notice), and every Group-of-Lots/Lot/Part column is **"—"** (not allowed). The spec's own cardinality legend defines `1` = "Mandatory & unique (only one)" and `—` = "Not allowed (0)".

> "This term refers to the type of procurement procedure… **It is marked for the whole Procedure with the `cbc:ProcedureCode` element**." *(§ Procedure Type (BT-105))*

And structurally, at the top of the same page:

> "**Procedure related information exists at the root of the notice**… Each **Group of Lots, Lot, and Part**, has its information in its dedicated `cac:ProcurementProjectLot` element…" *(Introduction)*

The XML element is `cbc:ProcedureCode` (a single root-level code), not a per-`ProcurementProjectLot` element — so a notice has **one** procedure type for its whole procedure; lots inherit it and cannot override it. The observed 0-mixed / 0-co-mingling result is exactly what the schema mandates.

(`ted-fields-reference.md` itself only says BT-105 "describes the **procurement procedure** used" — it doesn't spell out the level, which is why I confirmed against the primary eForms spec it cites.)

---

## Edge case found

**All-or-nothing NaN (no partial pattern).** `Procedure Type Code` is missing on **324 rows → 302 distinct awards → 194 notices**, and every one of those 194 notices is **entirely** NaN (no notice has some awards populated and others NaN — check 5 = 0). So the missingness is a *notice-level* "field not populated" event, not a per-award gap — consistent with BT-105 being declared once per notice. `Eu Funded`, by contrast, has **zero** NaNs.
